images.name: A Spring Afternoon in the Literature Club
images.description: In the clubroom on the third floor of the old Club Building, manuscript paper, back issues, and the sea breeze wait for the next round of proofreading.
images.background: The Literature Club's room is on the third floor of the old Club Building, where it keeps years of back issues and handwritten drafts. Short on members, the club is facing a merger review; its festival special issue, Spring Mint, carries the members' hope of being able to stay.
images.storyContext: A place for proofreading, interviews, and making things together, with room for a short silence too. The picture doesn't decide whether the special issue succeeds or whether the club keeps its room.
images.location: Haruka Academy · Literature Club, third floor of the old Club Building
visualNotes: An old wooden table, blank manuscript paper, and a blue volume make it clear what the room is for.
Rooftops, cherry blossoms, and the sea outside the window keep the feel of a seaside town in spring.
The room is empty; the furniture layout is this picture's own artistic take, best shown whole in the gallery.

images.name: An Afternoon of Proofreading Together
images.description: A mood piece: Mio Kamishiro sorts the manuscripts for the festival special issue, leaving room for the player's response and for the relationship to grow.
images.background: Mio Kamishiro is both class president of 2-B and president of the Literature Club, and she always thinks of other people's feelings first. Getting the festival special issue ready, she needs someone willing to take on some of the small jobs — and she'll remember every manuscript they worked on together.
images.storyContext: A moment of proofreading together that could happen. The empty chair leaves the player a place to join in, without fixing the player's looks, a romance, or any promise already made.
images.location: Haruka Academy · by the Literature Club's worktable
visualNotes: Mio's hairstyle, violet eyes, and navy sailor uniform follow her original portrait.
The pages she holds out, the pencil, and the empty chair are an invitation to work together.
Warm window light, cherry blossoms, and the sea keep the everyday mood fresh and age-appropriate.

images.name: Mio Kamishiro
images.description: Mio hugs books and papers to her chest; her shoulder-length black hair stands out against her dark sailor uniform, and her smile is faint.
images.background: Mio Kamishiro is class president of 2-B and president of the Literature Club. With the club facing a merger review, she is carrying the pressure of the festival special issue, Spring Mint, and of keeping the clubroom.
images.storyContext: For first meetings with the new student, class arrangements, or Literature Club conversations. Her politeness and smile don't mean the two of you are already close.
visualNotes: The books and manuscript pages are her identifying props; the unreadable pages should not be described as a finished special issue.

images.name: Rin Asakura
images.description: Rin winks and grins, a flower-shaped clip in her short auburn hair, holding a camera and her interview notebook at once.
images.background: Rin Asakura is a 2-B student and a News Club reporter. She's good at using interviews to get close to people; she's putting together the festival's Rumor Truth Wall, and has to face where the line is on what gets made public.
images.storyContext: Her default look — breezy and joking — for interview invitations and everyday chat. The smile doesn't mean she already knows the player's secrets.
visualNotes: The camera, interview notebook, armband, and flower clip keep her recognizable.

images.name: Kaho Shiina
images.description: Kaho holds an acoustic guitar and winks with a smile; her long light-brown hair falls beside a cream cardigan, with small ornaments in her hair.
images.background: Kaho Shiina is the Light Music Club's guitarist, in Class 2-A, and she's writing a new song that has no name yet. She acts on impulse and seems easygoing, but she's serious about the stage and about anyone willing to listen to her practice.
images.storyContext: For introducing rehearsals, stage prep, and after-school invitations. The guitar and the smile don't mean the new song is finished, or that she has already arranged to walk home with the player.
visualNotes: The acoustic guitar, cardigan, and hair ornaments carry over from her default design.

images.name: Yuma Shiraishi
images.description: Yuma, in glasses and a neat uniform, holds a clipboard, his expression quiet and serious.
images.background: Yuma Shiraishi is a 2-C student and the Student Council's vice president, in charge of club registration, budget reviews, and the festival schedule. He tends to show he cares through reminders and rules.
images.storyContext: For introducing him around club registration and Student Council business. Nothing on the clipboard confirms a review result, and his serious look doesn't mean he's hostile to the player.
visualNotes: Glasses, a striped tie, and the clipboard are what make him recognizable.

images.name: Haruka Mikoeda
images.description: Haruka holds a blue folder, her long hair half tied back and the Student Council badge pinned to her uniform; she looks calm.
images.background: Haruka Mikoeda is the third-year Student Council president, coordinating the festival's resources and schedule. Gentle and exact, she tends to steer an argument back to something that can actually be done.
images.storyContext: For scenes about budgets, clubrooms, and coordinating the festival. In the setting she is a supporting character; the portrait adds no romance route and no private promise.
visualNotes: The half-tied long hair, council badge, and blue folder follow her original portrait.

images.name: Chihiro Onodera
images.description: Ms. Onodera wears her hair in a low bun and a beige cardigan, holding up a piece of chalk in one hand and an open book in the other.
images.background: Chihiro Onodera is Class 2-B's homeroom teacher, teaches Japanese, and used to advise the Literature Club. She respects students' independence and understands the real pressure small clubs are under.
images.storyContext: For introducing the transfer student at the start, lessons, and gentle reminders. She offers guidance; the actual choice of club is still the student's.
visualNotes: Her adult face, the chalk, and the book mark her as a teacher; don't read her as a student in uniform.

images.name: Souta Morikawa
images.description: Souta raises a pair of drumsticks, white shirt sleeves rolled up and tie a little loose, with a big, cocky grin.
images.background: Souta Morikawa is the Light Music Club's drummer and Kaho's bandmate. Outgoing and quick with his mouth, he can liven up any room, and he can also cause misunderstandings by misreading a silence.
images.storyContext: For Light Music Club group scenes and introducing the stage prep. His relationship with Kaho is the bandmate one from the setting; the smile adds no rivalry and no romance.
visualNotes: The pair of drumsticks, short hair, and rolled-up sleeves keep him recognizable as the drummer.

images.name: Akane Toujou
images.description: Akane has long, straight dark hair and holds a blue hardcover, with a purple flower peeking out beside it; her gaze is quiet.
images.background: Akane Toujou is a third-year who chairs the Library Committee, and a regular at Umineko Bookstore. She treasures the old issues and the memories clubs leave behind, and shows she cares by saving seats, lending books, and keeping quiet company.
images.storyContext: She only enters the story naturally once the player walks into the library on their own. The portrait can introduce her, but it doesn't assume she has already saved the player a seat or told them about her family's past.
visualNotes: Keep the book and the flower as visual details, but nothing in the setting says where the flower came from, who gave it, or what it means.

images.name: Rin Asakura · Listening in Earnest
images.description: Rin has both eyes open and has put away the big grin; the camera and notebook are still at hand.
images.background: Rin Asakura is a 2-B student and a News Club reporter. She's good at using interviews to get close to people; she's putting together the festival's Rumor Truth Wall, and has to face where the line is on what gets made public.
images.storyContext: For conversations where Rin is really listening and thinking about where to draw the line on a story. It's only an expression variant: it doesn't mean any story has been held back or published.
visualNotes: The camera, interview notebook, armband, and flower clip keep her recognizable.

images.name: Kaho Shiina · Something on Her Mind
images.description: Kaho's blue eyes are wide open and her smile has faded; she's still in the cardigan, holding her guitar.
images.background: Kaho Shiina is the Light Music Club's guitarist, in Class 2-A, and she's writing a new song that has no name yet. She acts on impulse and seems easygoing, but she's serious about the stage and about anyone willing to listen to her practice.
images.storyContext: For conversations about rehearsal pressure or moments of hesitation. The current story has to supply what exactly she's worried about.
visualNotes: The acoustic guitar, cardigan, and hair ornaments carry over from her default design.

images.name: Chihiro Onodera · Off Duty, with a Book
images.description: Ms. Onodera has changed into a pale green coat and a long skirt, with a brown bag over her shoulder and the open book still in hand.
images.background: Chihiro Onodera is Class 2-B's homeroom teacher, teaches Japanese, and used to advise the Literature Club. She respects students' independence and understands the real pressure small clubs are under.
images.storyContext: For a casual appearance when the story calls for one. The change of clothes doesn't establish any meeting off campus, date, or family event.
visualNotes: She keeps her adult teacher's face and low bun; in the casual version the shoulder bag and the open book are the visible props.

images.name: Souta Morikawa · Ready to Rehearse
images.description: Souta wears a dark T-shirt under an open light-colored shirt, drumsticks still raised, his expression more restrained than in his uniform version.
images.background: Souta Morikawa is the Light Music Club's drummer and Kaho's bandmate. Outgoing and quick with his mouth, he can liven up any room, and he can also cause misunderstandings by misreading a silence.
images.storyContext: For the change of clothes and mood during Light Music Club rehearsals. The picture doesn't confirm how any rehearsal went, or that the festival performance has happened.
visualNotes: The drumsticks and hairstyle keep him recognizable; the dark T-shirt and open shirt set this apart from the uniform version.

images.name: Class 2-B · Day
images.description: Windows onto the sea, white curtains, and neat rows of desks fill the picture, with a stack of notebooks in the foreground and the blackboard on the right. Soft daylight fills the room.
images.background: Class 2-B is the transfer student's everyday home base; the player starts in the back row by the window. Cleaning duty, lunch breaks, study sessions, and the class's Sea Breeze Post booth for the festival all bring classmates together.
images.storyContext: The day view suits before class, breaks, and cleaning duty after school; the notebooks on the desk don't automatically belong to any character.
visualNotes: The window-side seats, the blackboard on the right, and the notebooks in the foreground are in the same place in the day and night pictures.

images.name: Class 2-B · Night
images.description: Windows onto the sea, white curtains, and neat rows of desks fill the picture, with a stack of notebooks in the foreground and the blackboard on the right. Warm lamplight and the blue-violet night light up the room.
images.background: Class 2-B is the transfer student's everyday home base; the player starts in the back row by the window. Cleaning duty, lunch breaks, study sessions, and the class's Sea Breeze Post booth for the festival all bring classmates together.
images.storyContext: The night view keeps the same classroom; only the lights inside and the bay outside have turned to night. The story still has to explain why someone is at school and what time it is — lit windows alone don't mean a date is happening.
visualNotes: The window-side seats, the blackboard on the right, and the notebooks in the foreground are in the same place in the day and night pictures.

images.name: Club Building · Day
images.description: The three-story wooden Club Building stands by the sea: a tiled roof, ivy climbing the right side, gravel out front, and a cherry tree make up the old building. Soft daylight fills the scene.
images.background: The Literature Club guards its back issues and manuscripts on the third floor; Light Music Club rehearsals, News Club work, and Student Council business all cross paths here too. Room assignments and the merger review make the old building a key place in the festival preparations.
images.storyContext: The day view suits visits before or after club activities. The exterior doesn't say whose room is behind each window.
visualNotes: Both the day and night versions keep the three floors, the ivy on the right, and the sea on the left.

images.name: Club Building · Night
images.description: The three-story wooden Club Building stands by the sea: a tiled roof, ivy climbing the right side, gravel out front, and a cherry tree make up the old building. Warm lamplight and the blue-violet night light up the scene.
images.background: The Literature Club guards its back issues and manuscripts on the third floor; Light Music Club rehearsals, News Club work, and Student Council business all cross paths here too. Room assignments and the merger review make the old building a key place in the festival preparations.
images.storyContext: The night view shows lit windows and the bay at nightfall. The windows are just atmosphere; they don't confirm the campus rumor about windows lit after 18:00 as anything supernatural.
visualNotes: Both the day and night versions keep the three floors, the ivy on the right, and the sea on the left.

images.name: Library · Day
images.description: A high-ceilinged reading room with an upper gallery; on the right a long table sits against windows facing the sea, and back issues are stacked on the low shelves. Soft daylight fills the room.
images.background: The library keeps the old festival special issues, and it's where Library Committee chair Akane Toujou enters the story naturally. Old issues, study sessions, and quiet time together set the pace of conversations here.
images.storyContext: The day view suits borrowing books, looking through old issues, and studying between classes. The empty seats in the picture aren't saved for the player or anyone else.
visualNotes: The gallery railing, the shelves, the long table on the right, and the stacks of books keep the same layout.

images.name: Library · Night
images.description: A high-ceilinged reading room with an upper gallery; on the right a long table sits against windows facing the sea, and back issues are stacked on the low shelves. Warm lamplight and the blue-violet night light up the room.
images.background: The library keeps the old festival special issues, and it's where Library Committee chair Akane Toujou enters the story naturally. Old issues, study sessions, and quiet time together set the pace of conversations here.
images.storyContext: In the night view the desk lamps and ceiling lights are on, with the bay at night outside. Going in or staying after dark has to fit the current schedule; the picture doesn't mean anyone has permission to stay in the library.
visualNotes: The gallery railing, the shelves, the long table on the right, and the stacks of books keep the same layout.

images.name: Sakurazaka Seawall · Day
images.description: Cherry trees arch over the slope down to the seawall, with the school fence and gate on the left and a white vending machine on the right, facing the sea breeze. Soft daylight fills the scene.
images.background: Sakurazaka Seawall links the walk home with a stop by the sea; it's a place for walking together, waiting, and talking about lyrics. With so few places to go after school in Seireki, chance meetings and rumors easily cross paths here.
images.storyContext: The day view works for walking home together or stopping for a moment. The picture shows a clear day; it doesn't show any of the rainy-day moments the setting allows for as having happened.
visualNotes: The fence on the left, the vending machine on the right, the seawall at the bottom of the slope, and the pavement stay in place.

images.name: Sakurazaka Seawall · Night
images.description: Cherry trees arch over the slope down to the seawall, with the school fence and gate on the left and a white vending machine on the right, facing the sea breeze. Warm lamplight and the blue-violet night light up the scene.
images.background: Sakurazaka Seawall links the walk home with a stop by the sea; it's a place for walking together, waiting, and talking about lyrics. With so few places to go after school in Seireki, chance meetings and rumors easily cross paths here.
images.storyContext: At night the streetlights and the vending machine are lit, and the slope is still dry. The story about drinks revealing who you like is a campus rumor; the picture doesn't prove it true.
visualNotes: The fence on the left, the vending machine on the right, the seawall at the bottom of the slope, and the pavement stay in place.

images.name: Seireki Town Shopping Street · Day
images.description: Books and flowerpots are displayed on the left side of the street; through the windows on the right you can see dining tables and guitars, and colorful awnings, bicycles, and the sea in the distance make an everyday street scene. Soft daylight fills the street.
images.background: There are only two shopping streets in front of Seireki's station, and the bookstore, restaurant, florist, and music shop are where students' after-school lives happen. The shops jointly sponsor the Evening Wind Lighting that closes the festival, and they're where clubs go to buy supplies.
images.storyContext: The day view suits shopping for supplies, browsing in the bookstore, and meeting up in a group. The shopfronts show what kind of street it is; don't invent new shop names from the blurry signs.
visualNotes: The bookstore and florist are on the left, the restaurant and music shop windows on the right, and the crossing and the sea in the distance line up in both versions.

images.name: Seireki Town Shopping Street · Night
images.description: Books and flowerpots are displayed on the left side of the street; through the windows on the right you can see dining tables and guitars, and colorful awnings, bicycles, and the sea in the distance make an everyday street scene. Warm lamplight and the blue-violet night light up the street.
images.background: There are only two shopping streets in front of Seireki's station, and the bookstore, restaurant, florist, and music shop are where students' after-school lives happen. The shops jointly sponsor the Evening Wind Lighting that closes the festival, and they're where clubs go to buy supplies.
images.storyContext: The night view keeps the same shopfronts; only the lighting and the sky change. Lit windows don't mean the Evening Wind Lighting closing ceremony has begun, and they don't show any shop's regular hours.
visualNotes: The bookstore and florist are on the left, the restaurant and music shop windows on the right, and the crossing and the sea in the distance line up in both versions.

images.name: Sea Breeze Across the Campus
images.description: Sunlight falls on a slope running down beside the classroom building; beyond the railing are cherry blossoms, green trees, the school's roofs, and the bay.
images.background: Haruka Academy sits on a gentle slope in Seireki, a small seaside town, its classroom building facing the harbor. The spring school festival is twenty-one days away, and a transfer student is about to start a new everyday life in Class 2-B.
images.storyContext: For the home page and the world introduction, setting the mood of a seaside campus, spring clubs, and everyday relationships. The empty scene doesn't assign the player a club or a romance.
visualNotes: This overview of the campus is shown separately from the five scene anchors; don't name the distant buildings as new story locations.
